title: Candidate 48 fails the vector-compensator alignment criterion despite containing the right carrier representation

claim.statement: The canonical candidate-48 vacuum does not realize a Lorentz-preserving MacDowell-Mansouri compensator in its singlet-to-active cross block.
claim.reason: The VEV has rank six, equally splits between Lorentz-scalar and Lorentz-vector directions of 2x5, and retains only a one-dimensional compact stabilizer.

setup.criterion: support entirely in the two SO(4)-scalar axes and rank-one vector alignment

interpretation: The abstract presence of 2x5 in the carrier is necessary but not sufficient for a compensator phase.
Half of the current cross-block order lies in Lorentz-vector directions, so the established SO(4) is explicitly/spontaneously reduced to the residual U(1).
Rank six is far from the aligned rank-one pattern required by the two-vector MacDowell-Mansouri toy.
A gravity-oriented branch must search for or engineer a different stationary vacuum rather than relabel candidate 48.
falsifiers: A basis-independent compensator identification must recover a six-dimensional Lorentz stabilizer; this cross block has dimension one.
A different vacuum on the candidate moduli could change the scalar/vector split and must be tested separately.
Other carrier blocks or composite constructions may supply a compensator and are not excluded.
nextBranches: Optimize over the exact candidate-48 moduli for maximum Lorentz-scalar fraction and stabilizer enhancement.
Add an invariant alignment potential for the two vector copies and re-solve stationarity.
Search other robust candidates for a rank-one timelike vector-5 cross-block VEV.
